How to train like a man
who wants to live long
Lift weights two or three times a week. Strength protects your joints, bones and posture as you age. It's the base of a long, active life.
Walk a lot every day. Eight to ten thousand steps keep your heart, mind and weight in good shape. It's the most underrated exercise there is.
Do some cardio that makes you breathe hard. Running, cycling, swimming, rowing. A strong heart and lungs are worth more than big arms.
Stretch and move your joints daily. Hips, back, shoulders. Ten minutes of mobility keeps you moving freely at sixty and beyond.
Before: I only trained my body. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I train my mind too, because both need it to last.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I only trained my body. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I train my mind too, because both need it to last.

slides.texte_overlay: Train your balance. Stand on one leg, walk on uneven ground, do yoga. Good balance prevents falls and injuries later in life.
Recover as seriously as you train. Sleep, rest days and good food are where your body actually gets stronger. Rest is training too.
